ceiling_respected: 8 is the settled cap the manifest already binds, so this stays inside the authorized execution parameters and needs no new execution identity. Going above 8 would require a new manifest and a fresh owner authorization.
how_it_will_be_checked: gemma's abandonment rate and the cells/hour rate are compared over a window after this change against the same measures before it. If abandonment rises materially without a throughput gain, the pin is reverted by a further amendment rather than left in place. This is a measurement, not a setting.
note: Append-only. Amends an earlier override; grants no new spend authority and changes no cap. The execution identity is unchanged.
the_risk_this_takes: This may be SLOWER rather than faster. gemma is already returning 429 rate limits at concurrency 1, and 8x the request rate against a rate-limited endpoint can cost more in retries and backoff than parallelism gains. The measured gemma abandonment rate before this change is the comparison point: 57.1% during the degraded window, about 20% cumulative once it recovered.
what_it_still_does_not_settle: the main run's cap. That needs its own measurement under its own manifest; a width that works for 945 canary cells is evidence, not authorization.
why: Schedule. At gemma concurrency 1 the main run projects to 14.2 days of continuous running, because gemma carries about 95% of all call time and pinning it makes that share effectively serial. At concurrency 8 the same grid is 2.4 days. The owner's instruction is to go as fast as the provider allows.
